items.titleEn: Chevron shares rise after third-quarter profit jumps nearly 200%
items.summaryEn: Buy Chevron (CVX). Earnings beat is driven by downstream: refining margins surged as Russia/Middle East attacks tightened diesel/jet supply, and Chevron ran US refineries at ~98% capacity with >10% yield gains. Strong cash flow (CFO $16B, adjusted FCF $14.2B) plus net debt down to $20.7B supports dividends and buybacks, so the market reaction should persist beyond the quarter if disruptions keep margins elevated. Key Risk: Refining margins mean-revert fast as supply disruptions ease and utilization/yields fall, wiping out the earnings driver. Buy Exxon Mobil (XOM). If refining margins are the real engine across majors, XOM’s earnings power should benefit alongside CVX, and the group’s cash generation supports continued capital returns. The thesis is sector-wide downstream strength, not just Chevron-specific execution.

items.titleEn: 'Microsoft set to soar, Alphabet won't rally': Jim Cramer explains why
items.summaryEn: Buy Microsoft (MSFT). The setup is clear: accelerating Azure (48% growth) plus strong cloud revenue and positive free cash flow while still scaling AI (Copilot traction). The market is rewarding “spend with discipline,” so MSFT should keep rerating upward as investors gain confidence AI spend is producing returns. Key Risk: Azure growth decelerates sharply or Copilot adoption disappoints, forcing Microsoft to spend more without improving free cash flow. Sell Alphabet (GOOGL). The news flow is negative on the core issue: heavy AI infrastructure spend drove negative free cash flow (-$9.07B) and search growth slowed (12% vs 17%). Even with Google Cloud doubling, it isn’t enough to offset the cost and search pressure, so the stock likely stays under pressure until estimates and valuation reset.

items.titleEn: Nvidia's web of AI bets: Smart strategy or bubble risk?
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Nvidia's $3 billion investment in Meta's share sale, announced Tuesday, is the latest addition to a portfolio of stakes, loans and guarantees that has made the chip giant what some analysts describe as the central bank of the artificial intelligence boom. The galaxy of deals has helped keep demand running high for Nvidia's processors, which power vast data centers around the world and are the central ingredient of the AI revolution.
